title: Tip on how to work with Meshy.ai
author: PicaloShmikalo
selftext:
I spent the last 2 days how to generate assets for games in Meshy, I started with Meshy for Smart topology but results were with artifacts and holes. It is too hard to fix it.  
After struggle I used High details models, it generated 1M vertices, clearly not ready for game, people who know Blend can fix it, but I wanted to automate it. I have created a prompt that do that for me.

>I have a high-poly model with approximately 1,000,000 vertices currently selected in the scene. Please write and execute a Blender Python (bpy) script to optimize it down to 50,000 vertices while preserving its surface details and baking all essential PBR textures (Diffuse, Roughness, and Normal). Execute the following steps in order:   
1. Duplicate the currently selected active object.   
2. Rename the original object to "Model\_HighPoly" and hide it completely from both the viewport and renders.   
3. Rename the duplicated object to "Model\_LowPoly" and ensure it is the active selection.   
4. Add a Decimate modifier to "Model\_LowPoly". Set the mode to 'Collapse' and the ratio to 0.05. Apply the modifier.   
5. Shade "Model\_LowPoly" smooth.   
6. Unwrap the UVs of "Model\_LowPoly" using Smart UV Project.   
7. Create a new material for "Model\_LowPoly".   
8. Inside this new material, create three separate 2048x2048 Image Texture nodes named "Bake\_Diffuse", "Bake\_Roughness", and "Bake\_Normal". Set the color space for Roughness and Normal to 'Non-Color'. 9. Switch the scene's render engine to Cycles.   
10. Configure the bake settings to bake from "Selected to Active" with a small extrusion value (e.g., 0.01m) to prevent ray misses.   
11. Sequentially bake the maps from the hidden "Model\_HighPoly" to "Model\_LowPoly": - Make the "Bake\_Diffuse" node active, set bake type to 'DIFFUSE' (turn off Direct and Indirect lighting contributions), and execute the bake. - Make the "Bake\_Roughness" node active, set bake type to 'ROUGHNESS', and execute the bake. - Make the "Bake\_Normal" node active, set bake type to 'NORMAL', and execute the bake.   
12. Connect the newly baked image textures to their respective sockets (Base Color, Roughness, and Normal via a Normal Map node) on the Principled BSDF of "Model\_LowPoly". Once complete, output a success message in our chat confirming the final vertex count of "Model\_LowPoly" and that all three textures were successfully baked.

Would appreciate more tips from you to share here.
